doc.dbt.__overview__.block_contents:
### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand` button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build, or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.

---

### More information

- Read the [dbt viewpoint](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/viewpoint)
- [Installation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/installation)
- Join the [dbt Community](https://www.getdbt.com/community/) for questions and discussion

model.pilot_shop.customers.compiled_code:
with signed_up as (

    -- Everyone who has signed up, whether or not they have ordered

    select * from "pilot"."main"."stg_customers"

),

spending as (

    select
        customer_id,
        count(distinct order_id) > 1 as has_ordered_again,
        count(distinct order_id) as order_count,
        min(ordered_at) as first_ordered_at,
        sum(order_total) as total_spent
    from "pilot"."main"."orders"
    group by customer_id

),

profiles as (

    select
        signed_up.*,
        coalesce(spending.total_spent, 0) as lifetime_spend,
        coalesce(spending.order_count, 0) as order_count,
        spending.first_ordered_at,
        case when spending.has_ordered_again then 'regular' else 'new' end as customer_type
    from signed_up
    left join spending on spending.customer_id = signed_up.customer_id

)

select * from profiles

    where date_day < cast('2026-12-31' as date)

)

model.pilot_shop.order_items.compiled_code:
-- One row per product on an order, priced, with when the order was placed.

with lines as (

    select * from "pilot"."main"."stg_order_lines"

),

placed as (

    select order_id, ordered_at from "pilot"."main"."stg_orders"

),

products as (

    select * from "pilot"."main"."stg_products"

)

select
    lines.order_line_id,
    lines.order_id,
    placed.ordered_at,
    lines.product_sku,
    products.category,
    products.is_drink,
    lines.quantity,
    lines.quantity * products.unit_price as line_total
from lines
inner join placed on placed.order_id = lines.order_id
inner join products on products.product_sku = lines.product_sku

model.pilot_shop.orders.compiled_code:
-- One row per order, with how much was on it.

with placed as (

    select * from "pilot"."main"."stg_orders"

),

baskets as (

    select
        order_id,
        count(*) as line_count,
        sum(quantity) as item_count,
        sum(case when is_drink then quantity else 0 end) as drink_count
    from "pilot"."main"."order_items"
    group by order_id

)

select
    placed.*,
    coalesce(baskets.line_count, 0) as line_count,
    coalesce(baskets.item_count, 0) as item_count,
    coalesce(baskets.drink_count, 0) as drink_count
from placed
left join baskets on baskets.order_id = placed.order_id

model.pilot_shop.stg_orders.compiled_code:
-- Orders as the till records them: one row per order, money in dollars.

with till as (

    select * from "pilot"."main_raw"."raw_orders"

)

select
    id as order_id,
    customer_id,
    location_id,
    cast(ordered_at as timestamp) as ordered_at,
    
    (subtotal_cents / 100.0)
 as subtotal,
    
    (tax_cents / 100.0)
 as tax_paid,
    
    ((subtotal_cents + tax_cents) / 100.0)
 as order_total
from till
